Text:
# Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) under Partial Segment Blockage Disruptions

## 1. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $T$ | Set of trains, indexed by $t$ |
| $S$ | Set of stations (including origins and destinations), indexed by $s$ |
| $A$ | Set of arcs (segments between consecutive stations), $A = \{(i,j) \mid i,j \in S,\, i \neq j\}$, indexed by $(i,j)$ |
| $D \subseteq A$ | Set of disruption-affected arcs (partially blocked segments) |
| $K$ | Set of discretized speed profile segments, indexed by $k$ |
| $B$ | Set of bidirectional train pairs that may conflict on shared tracks, indexed by $(t_1, t_2)$ |
| $P_t$ | Set of feasible paths for train $t$ (normal path and rerouted path) |

## 2. Parameters

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $t_{ij}^{\min},\; t_{ij}^{\max}$ | Minimum and maximum running time on arc $(i,j)$ |
| $t_s^{\min},\; t_s^{\max}$ | Minimum and maximum dwell time at station $s$ |
| $T_{\text{start}},\; T_{\text{end}}$ | Planning horizon start and end times |
| $M$ | Sufficiently large constant (Big-M) |
| $c_{\text{delay}}$ | Penalty cost coefficient for train delay |
| $c_{\text{energy}}$ | Cost coefficient for energy consumption |
| $c_{\text{cancel}}$ | Penalty cost coefficient for train cancellation |
| $c_{\text{reroute}}$ | Penalty cost coefficient for train rerouting |
| $v_k$ | Speed level for speed segment $k$ |
| $E_k$ | Energy consumption for speed segment $k$ |
| $L_{ij}$ | Length of arc $(i,j)$ |
| $d_{ij}$ | Disruption duration for arc $(i,j) \in D$ |
| $w_{\text{start}},\; w_{\text{end}}$ | Disruption time window start and end |
| $h_{\min}$ | Minimum headway between trains on the same arc |
| $\text{cap}_s$ | Maximum number of trains at station $s$ simultaneously |
| $\text{cap}_{ij}$ | Maximum number of trains on arc $(i,j)$ simultaneously |
| $o_t$ | Origin station of train $t$ |
| $f_t$ | Destination station of train $t$ |
| $\mathcal{A}_t^{\text{norm}}$ | Set of arcs on the normal path of train $t$ |
| $\mathcal{A}_t^{\text{rer}}$ | Set of arcs on the rerouted path of train $t$ |
| $\tau_{t}^{\text{sch}}$ | Scheduled arrival time of train $t$ at its destination |

## 3. Decision Variables

### Binary Variables

| Variable | Domain | Description |
|----------|--------|-------------|
| $x_t$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $t$ is cancelled, 0 otherwise |
| $y_t$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $t$ is rerouted, 0 otherwise |
| $r_{t,ij}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $t$ traverses arc $(i,j)$ in the normal direction, 0 otherwise |
| $q_{t,ij}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $t$ traverses arc $(i,j)$ in the rerouted (opposite) direction, 0 otherwise |
| $z_{t,ij}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $t$ passes through arc $(i,j)$ during the disruption window, 0 otherwise |
| $s_{t,ij,k}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $t$ uses speed segment $k$ on arc $(i,j)$, 0 otherwise |
| $p_{t_1 t_2, ij}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $t_1$ precedes train $t_2$ on arc $(i,j)$, 0 otherwise (for $t_1 \neq t_2$) |

### Continuous Variables

| Variable | Domain | Description |
|----------|--------|-------------|
| $a_{t,s}$ | $[0,\, T_{\text{end}}]$ | Arrival time of train $t$ at station $s$ |
| $d_{t,s}$ | $[0,\, T_{\text{end}}]$ | Departure time of train $t$ from station $s$ |
| $o_{t,ij}$ | $[0,\, T_{\text{end}}]$ | Running time of train $t$ on arc $(i,j)$ |
| $e_t$ | $[0,\, \infty)$ | Total energy consumption of train $t$ |
| $\text{delay}_t$ | $[0,\, \infty)$ | Total delay of train $t$ at its destination |

## 4. Objective Function

Minimize the total operational cost, which comprises delay penalties, energy consumption costs, cancellation penalties, and rerouting penalties:

$$
\min \; Z = \sum_{t \in T} \left( c_{\text{delay}} \cdot \text{delay}_t + c_{\text{energy}} \cdot e_t + c_{\text{cancel}} \cdot x_t + c_{\text{reroute}} \cdot y_t \right)
$$

## 5. Constraints

### 5.1 Train Cancellation Constraints

If a train is cancelled, all its arrival and departure times are deactivated:

$$
a_{t,s} \leq M \cdot (1 - x_t) \quad \forall\, t \in T,\; s \in S
$$

$$
d_{t,s} \leq M \cdot (1 - x_t) \quad \forall\, t \in T,\; s \in S
$$

### 5.2 Rerouting and Path Selection Constraints

For each disruption-affected arc, a non-cancelled train must choose exactly one direction (normal or rerouted):

$$
r_{t,ij} + q_{t,ij} = 1 - x_t \quad \forall\, t \in T,\; (i,j) \in D
$$

For non-disruption arcs, only the normal direction is available:

$$
r_{t,ij} = 1 - x_t, \quad q_{t,ij} = 0 \quad \forall\, t \in T,\; (i,j) \in A \setminus D
$$

Rerouting consistency: if a train is rerouted, it must use the rerouted direction on all disruption arcs; if not rerouted, it must use the normal direction:

$$
q_{t,ij} \geq y_t - x_t \quad \forall\, t \in T,\; (i,j) \in D
$$

$$
r_{t,ij} \geq 1 - y_t - x_t \quad \forall\, t \in T,\; (i,j) \in D
$$

### 5.3 Time Consistency (Flow) Constraints

The arrival time at the downstream station must equal the departure time from the upstream station plus the running time on the connecting arc:

$$
a_{t,j} \geq d_{t,i} + o_{t,ij} - M \cdot (1 - r_{t,ij}) - M \cdot (1 - q_{t,ij}) \quad \forall\, t \in T,\; (i,j) \in A
$$

$$
a_{t,j} \leq d_{t,i} + o_{t,ij} + M \cdot (1 - r_{t,ij}) + M \cdot (1 - q_{t,ij}) \quad \forall\, t \in T,\; (i,j) \in A
$$

### 5.4 Dwell Time Constraints

At intermediate stations, the departure time must respect minimum and maximum dwell times:

$$
d_{t,s} \geq a_{t,s} + t_s^{\min} - M \cdot x_t \quad \forall\, t \in T,\; s \in S \setminus \{o_t, f_t\}
$$

$$
d_{t,s} \leq a_{t,s} + t_s^{\max} + M \cdot x_t \quad \forall\, t \in T,\; s \in S \setminus \{o_t, f_t\}
$$

### 5.5 Running Time Bounds

The running time on each arc must lie within feasible bounds, linked to the arc usage:

$$
o_{t,ij} \geq t_{ij}^{\min} \cdot (r_{t,ij} + q_{t,ij}) - M \cdot x_t \quad \forall\, t \in T,\; (i,j) \in A
$$

$$
o_{t,ij} \leq t_{ij}^{\max} \cdot (r_{t,ij} + q_{t,ij}) + M \cdot x_t \quad \forall\, t \in T,\; (i,j) \in A
$$

### 5.6 Disruption Window Constraints

A train traversing a disruption arc during the disruption window must account for the blockage duration. The binary $z_{t,ij}$ indicates whether the train is in the disruption window:

$$
z_{t,ij} \leq r_{t,ij} + q_{t,ij} \quad \forall\, t \in T,\; (i,j) \in D
$$

$$
z_{t,ij} \leq 1 - y_t + x_t \quad \forall\, t \in T,\; (i,j) \in D
$$

The running time on a disruption arc must include the disruption duration if the train passes through during the window:

$$
o_{t,ij} \geq d_{ij} \cdot z_{t,ij} - M \cdot x_t \quad \forall\, t \in T,\; (i,j) \in D
$$

### 5.7 Speed Profile Selection Constraints

Each non-cancelled train using an arc must select exactly one speed segment:

$$
\sum_{k \in K} s_{t,ij,k} = r_{t,ij} + q_{t,ij} \quad \forall\, t \in T,\; (i,j) \in A
$$

### 5.8 Energy Consumption Constraints

The total energy consumption of each train is the sum of the energy of the selected speed segments across all arcs:

$$
e_t = \sum_{(i,j) \in A} \sum_{k \in K} E_k \cdot s_{t,ij,k} \quad \forall\, t \in T
$$

### 5.9 Running Time–Speed Coupling Constraints

The running time on an arc is determined by the selected speed segment. Assuming the running time for speed segment $k$ on arc $(i,j)$ is $\tau_{ij,k}$ (a precomputed parameter based on arc length and speed profile):

$$
o_{t,ij} = \sum_{k \in K} \tau_{ij,k} \cdot s_{t,ij,k} \quad \forall\, t \in T,\; (i,j) \in A
$$

### 5.10 Train Ordering and Headway Constraints

For any pair of trains $t_1, t_2$ on the same arc $(i,j)$, one must precede the other, and the minimum headway must be maintained. Introduce ordering binary $p_{t_1 t_2, ij}$:

$$
p_{t_1 t_2, ij} + p_{t_2 t_1, ij} \leq 1 \quad \forall\, (t_1, t_2) \in T \times T,\; t_1 \neq t_2,\; (i,j) \in A
$$

If $t_1$ precedes $t_2$ on arc $(i,j)$:

$$
d_{t_2, i} \geq d_{t_1, i} + h_{\min} - M \cdot (1 - p_{t_1 t_2, ij}) - M \cdot x_{t_1} - M \cdot x_{t_2} \quad \forall\, t_1 \neq t_2,\; (i,j) \in A
$$

If $t_2$ precedes $t_1$ on arc $(i,j)$:

$$
d_{t_1, i} \geq d_{t_2, i} + h_{\min} - M \cdot (1 - p_{t_2 t_1, ij}) - M \cdot x_{t_1} - M \cdot x_{t_2} \quad \forall\, t_1 \neq t_2,\; (i,j) \in A
$$

### 5.11 Bidirectional Conflict Resolution on Shared Tracks

For bidirectional train pairs $(t_1, t_2) \in B$ sharing a track in the disruption area, the trains must not occupy the shared segment simultaneously. This is enforced through the headway constraints above combined with the rerouting logic: if both trains are rerouted onto the same physical track in opposite directions, the ordering and headway constraints ensure temporal separation.

$$
d_{t_2, i} \geq d_{t_1, i} + h_{\min} - M \cdot (1 - p_{t_1 t_2, ij}) - M \cdot x_{t_1} - M \cdot x_{t_2} \quad \forall\, (t_1, t_2) \in B,\; (i,j) \in D
$$

### 5.12 Planning Horizon Constraints

All arrival and departure times must fall within the planning horizon:

$$
T_{\text{start}} - M \cdot x_t \leq a_{t,s} \leq T_{\text{end}} \quad \forall\, t \in T,\; s \in S
$$

$$
T_{\text{start}} - M \cdot x_t \leq d_{t,s} \leq T_{\text{end}} \quad \forall\, t \in T,\; s \in S
$$

### 5.13 Delay Definition

The delay of each train is measured at its destination relative to the scheduled arrival time:

$$
\text{delay}_t \geq a_{t, f_t} - \tau_t^{\text{sch}} - M \cdot x_t \quad \forall\, t \in T
$$

$$
\text{delay}_t \geq 0 \quad \forall\, t \in T
$$

### 5.14 Station Capacity Constraints

The number of trains simultaneously at any station must not exceed the station capacity. This is approximated by limiting the total number of non-cancelled trains that visit each station:

$$
\sum_{t \in T} (1 - x_t) \cdot \mathbb{1}[s \in \text{path}(t)] \leq \text{cap}_s \cdot |T| \quad \forall\, s \in S
$$

*(Assumption: This is a simplified capacity constraint. A full time-indexed formulation would require discretizing time and tracking train presence at each time step.)*

### 5.15 Track Capacity Constraints

The number of trains simultaneously on any arc must not exceed the track capacity:

$$
\sum_{t \in T} (r_{t,ij} + q_{t,ij}) \leq \text{cap}_{ij} \quad \forall\, (i,j) \in A
$$

### 5.16 Variable Domain Constraints

$$
x_t, \; y_t, \; r_{t,ij}, \; q_{t,ij}, \; z_{t,ij}, \; s_{t,ij,k}, \; p_{t_1 t_2, ij} \in \{0, 1\}
$$

$$
a_{t,s}, \; d_{t,s}, \; o_{t,ij}, \; e_t, \; \text{delay}_t \geq 0
$$

## 6. Key Assumptions

1. **Discretized speed profiles**: The continuous speed profile is approximated by a finite set of precomputed speed segments $K$, each with a fixed energy consumption $E_k$ and running time $\tau_{ij,k}$. This linearizes the otherwise nonlinear relationship between speed, energy, and running time.
2. **Single disruption window**: There is one disruption time window $[w_{\text{start}}, w_{\text{end}}]$ affecting a set of arcs $D$.
3. **Binary rerouting decision**: Each train is either fully rerouted or not; partial rerouting is not considered.
4. **Simplified capacity constraints**: Station and track capacities are modeled as aggregate constraints rather than time-indexed occupancy constraints, which is a reasonable simplification for a MILP formulation.
5. **Precedence-based headway**: Train conflicts are resolved through pairwise ordering variables and minimum headway constraints, rather than a full time-space network formulation.
6. **Energy is additive**: Total energy consumption is the sum of per-arc, per-speed-segment energy values, with no coupling between consecutive arcs (e.g., no momentum carry-over effects).
7. **Big-M formulation**: The model uses Big-M constants to linearize logical implications. The value of $M$ must be chosen sufficiently large to not cut off feasible solutions but as small as possible for computational efficiency.

Based on the provided input, here is a complete Mixed-Integer Linear Programming (MILP) model for the **Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP)** under partial segment blockages.

### 1. Problem Description and Assumptions

**Problem Context:**
A high-speed railway network experiences a partial segment blockage. One track in a specific segment is unavailable for a defined time window. Trains must be rescheduled (adjusting times, orders, and routes) and their speed profiles optimized to minimize total cost (delays and energy consumption) while ensuring conflict-free operation.

**Key Assumptions:**
1.  **Network Structure:** The railway is modeled as a directed graph $G=(N, A)$, where $N$ is the set of nodes (stations and block sections) and $A$ is the set of arcs (track segments).
2.  **Disruption:** A specific arc $a_{dis}$ is blocked for trains traveling in direction $d_{dis}$ during time window $[T_{start}, T_{end}]$. Trains in this direction must reroute to the opposite track (if available and feasible) or wait. *Assumption: The opposite track is available for bidirectional traffic during the disruption, but with reduced capacity or specific signaling constraints.*
3.  **Train Dynamics:** Train movement is governed by physics. To linearize the model, we assume that for each arc, the running time is a function of the entry speed and exit speed. We approximate the energy consumption and running time using piecewise linear functions or assume a fixed set of feasible "speed profiles" (plans) for each arc, as hinted by the "train plan selection" in the text. *Assumption: We use a discretized set of feasible speed profiles (plans) for each arc to maintain linearity.*
4.  **Conflict Resolution:** Conflicts are resolved using a "First-In-First-Out" (FIFO) or "Ordering" variable approach. We assume that on any single track segment, trains cannot overtake each other (no passing).
5.  **Objective:** Minimize the weighted sum of total passenger delay and total energy consumption.
6.  **Linearity:** All non-linear relationships (e.g., energy vs. speed) are linearized using piecewise linear approximations or pre-computed discrete plans.

---

### 2. Sets and Indices

*   $T$: Set of trains.
*   $N$: Set of nodes (stations and block sections).
*   $A$: Set of arcs (track segments).
*   $A_{in}(n)$: Set of arcs entering node $n$.
*   $A_{out}(n)$: Set of arcs leaving node $n$.
*   $P_{t,a}$: Set of feasible speed profiles (plans) for train $t$ on arc $a$.
*   $D$: Set of directions (e.g., Up, Down).
*   $A_{dis}$: The specific arc affected by the disruption.
*   $[T_{start}, T_{end}]$: The disruption time window.

### 3. Parameters

*   $S_{t,n}$: Scheduled arrival time of train $t$ at node $n$.
*   $D_{t,n}$: Scheduled departure time of train $t$ from node $n$.
*   $R_{t,a}$: Scheduled running time of train $t$ on arc $a$.
*   $E_{t,a}^{sched}$: Scheduled energy consumption of train $t$ on arc $a$.
*   $w_{delay}$: Weight for delay cost.
*   $w_{energy}$: Weight for energy cost.
*   $M$: A large constant (Big-M) for linearization.
*   $L_{a}$: Length of arc $a$.
*   $v_{max}$: Maximum speed limit.
*   $v_{min}$: Minimum speed limit.
*   $a_{max}$: Maximum acceleration.
*   $b_{max}$: Maximum braking deceleration.
*   $h_{a}$: Minimum headway (time gap) between two trains on arc $a$.
*   $h_{n}^{arr}$: Minimum arrival headway at node $n$.
*   $h_{n}^{dep}$: Minimum departure headway at node $n$.
*   $x_{t,a}^{plan}$: Binary variable indicating if train $t$ uses plan $p$ on arc $a$.
*   $r_{t,a}^{p}$: Running time of train $t$ on arc $a$ using plan $p$.
*   $e_{t,a}^{p}$: Energy consumption of train $t$ on arc $a$ using plan $p$.
*   $v_{t,a}^{p, in}$: Entry speed of train $t$ on arc $a$ using plan $p$.
*   $v_{t,a}^{p, out}$: Exit speed of train $t$ on arc $a$ using plan $p$.

### 4. Decision Variables

**Continuous Variables:**
*   $Arr_{t,n}$: Actual arrival time of train $t$ at node $n$.
*   $Dep_{t,n}$: Actual departure time of train $t$ from node $n$.
*   $Run_{t,a}$: Actual running time of train $t$ on arc $a$.
*   $Energy_{t,a}$: Actual energy consumption of train $t$ on arc $a$.
*   $Delay_{t,n}^{arr}$: Arrival delay of train $t$ at node $n$.
*   $Delay_{t,n}^{dep}$: Departure delay of train $t$ from node $n$.

**Binary Variables:**
*   $y_{t,a}^{p} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $t$ selects speed profile (plan) $p$ for arc $a$, 0 otherwise.
*   $z_{t,a}^{dis} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $t$ is affected by the disruption on arc $a$ (i.e., must reroute or wait), 0 otherwise.
*   $u_{t,a}^{dir} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $t$ uses the opposite track (reroutes) on arc $a$ during the disruption, 0 otherwise.
*   $o_{t,t',a} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $t$ precedes train $t'$ on arc $a$, 0 otherwise. (Used for ordering).
*   $c_{t,n} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $t$ is cancelled at node $n$ (optional, assuming no cancellations for simplicity, but can be added). *Assumption: No cancellations allowed in this model.*

---

### 5. Objective Function

Minimize the total cost, which is the weighted sum of total delay and total energy consumption:

$$
\min Z = w_{delay} \sum_{t \in T} \sum_{n \in N} (Delay_{t,n}^{arr} + Delay_{t,n}^{dep}) + w_{energy} \sum_{t \in T} \sum_{a \in A} Energy_{t,a}
$$

---

### 6. Constraints

#### 6.1. Train Dynamics and Speed Profile Selection

For each train $t$ and arc $a$, exactly one speed profile must be selected:

$$
\sum_{p \in P_{t,a}} y_{t,a}^{p} = 1, \quad \forall t \in T, a \in A
$$

The running time and energy consumption are determined by the selected plan:

$$
Run_{t,a} = \sum_{p \in P_{t,a}} r_{t,a}^{p} y_{t,a}^{p}, \quad \forall t \in T, a \in A
$$

$$
Energy_{t,a} = \sum_{p \in P_{t,a}} e_{t,a}^{p} y_{t,a}^{p}, \quad \forall t \in T, a \in A
$$

#### 6.2. Time-Linking Constraints (Flow Conservation)

The departure time from a node must equal the arrival time plus the dwell time. The arrival time at a node must equal the departure time from the previous node plus the running time.

For each train $t$ and node $n$ (except the origin):
$$
Arr_{t,n} = \sum_{a \in A_{in}(n)} (Dep_{t, tail(a)} + Run_{t,a}) \cdot \delta_{t,a,n}
$$
*Note: To simplify, we assume a fixed path for each train (no dynamic rerouting of the entire path, only local rerouting on the disrupted arc). If the path is fixed, we can write:*

$$
Arr_{t,n} = Dep_{t, n_{prev}} + Run_{t, a_{prev}}, \quad \forall t \in T, n \in N \setminus \{Origin\}
$$

$$
Dep_{t,n} = Arr_{t,n} + Dwell_{t,n}, \quad \forall t \in T, n \in N
$$

*Assumption: Dwell times are fixed or have minimum/maximum bounds. Let $Dwell_{min,t,n}$ and $Dwell_{max,t,n}$ be the bounds.*

$$
Dwell_{min,t,n} \leq Dep_{t,n} - Arr_{t,n} \leq Dwell_{max,t,n}, \quad \forall t \in T, n \in N
$$

#### 6.3. Disruption and Rerouting Constraints

If a train $t$ is scheduled to traverse the disrupted arc $a_{dis}$ during the disruption window $[T_{start}, T_{end}]$, it must either wait or reroute.

Let $t_{enter}^{t, a_{dis}}$ be the time train $t$ enters arc $a_{dis}$.
Let $t_{exit}^{t, a_{dis}}$ be the time train $t$ exits arc $a_{dis}$.

If $t_{enter}^{t, a_{dis}} < T_{end}$ and $t_{exit}^{t, a_{dis}} > T_{start}$, the train is affected.

**Rerouting Logic:**
If train $t$ is in direction $d_{dis}$ and affected, it must use the opposite track. This implies a change in the arc used. Let $a_{opposite}$ be the parallel arc in the opposite direction.

$$
u_{t, a_{dis}}^{dir} = 1 \implies \text{Train } t \text{ uses } a_{opposite} \text{ instead of } a_{dis}
$$

To linearize this, we can enforce that if the train's scheduled time overlaps with the disruption, it must select a plan on the opposite track or wait.

*Assumption: We model the rerouting as a choice of arc. If $t$ is affected, it cannot use $a_{dis}$.*

$$
Run_{t, a_{dis}} = 0 \quad \text{if } t \text{ is affected and reroutes}
$$

A more robust linear formulation for the disruption constraint:

For any train $t$ in direction $d_{dis}$:
$$
Arr_{t, head(a_{dis})} \geq T_{end} + M(1 - z_{t, a_{dis}}^{dis})
$$
$$
Arr_{t, head(a_{dis})} \leq T_{start} - M(1 - z_{t, a_{dis}}^{dis})
$$
$$
z_{t, a_{dis}}^{dis} \in \{0,1\}
$$

If $z_{t, a_{dis}}^{dis} = 1$, the train is "affected" and must reroute. If $z_{t, a_{dis}}^{dis} = 0$, the train is not affected (arrives before or after the window).

If $z_{t, a_{dis}}^{dis} = 1$, the train must use the opposite track $a_{opp}$.
$$
Run_{t, a_{dis}} = 0, \quad \forall t \in T, a = a_{dis} \text{ if } z_{t, a_{dis}}^{dis}=1
$$
$$
Run_{t, a_{opp}} > 0, \quad \forall t \in T, a = a_{opp} \text{ if } z_{t, a_{dis}}^{dis}=1
$$

*Note: This requires defining the network such that $a_{dis}$ and $a_{opp}$ are parallel arcs between the same nodes.*

#### 6.4. Conflict Resolution (Headway Constraints)

Trains cannot occupy the same track segment at the same time. We use ordering variables $o_{t,t',a}$.

For any two trains $t, t' \in T$ ($t \neq t'$) and arc $a \in A$:

If $o_{t,t',a} = 1$, train $t$ precedes train $t'$ on arc $a$.
$$
Dep_{t', tail(a)} \geq Dep_{t, tail(a)} + h_{a} + M(1 - o_{t,t',a})
$$
$$
Dep_{t', tail(a)} \leq Dep_{t, tail(a)} + h_{a} - M o_{t,t',a}
$$

*Note: This ensures that if $o_{t,t',a}=1$, the departure of $t'$ is at least $h_a$ after the departure of $t$. If $o_{t,t',a}=0$, the reverse is true.*

We must ensure that for any pair, one precedes the other:
$$
o_{t,t',a} + o_{t',t,a} = 1, \quad \forall t \neq t', a \in A
$$

**Node Conflicts:**
Similar constraints apply for arrival and departure at nodes $n$:
$$
Arr_{t', n} \geq Arr_{t, n} + h_{n}^{arr} + M(1 - o_{t,t',n}^{arr})
$$
$$
Arr_{t', n} \leq Arr_{t, n} + h_{n}^{arr} - M o_{t,t',n}^{arr}
$$
$$
o_{t,t',n}^{arr} + o_{t',t,n}^{arr} = 1
$$

#### 6.5. Delay Calculation

$$
Delay_{t,n}^{arr} \geq Arr_{t,n} - S_{t,n}, \quad \forall t \in T, n \in N
$$
$$
Delay_{t,n}^{arr} \geq 0, \quad \forall t \in T, n \in N
$$

$$
Delay_{t,n}^{dep} \geq Dep_{t,n} - D_{t,n}, \quad \forall t \in T, n \in N
$$
$$
Delay_{t,n}^{dep} \geq 0, \quad \forall t \in T, n \in N
$$

#### 6.6. Speed Profile Feasibility (Physics Constraints)

The pre-computed plans $P_{t,a}$ must satisfy physical constraints. Since we select from a pre-computed set, these are implicitly satisfied. However, if we were to generate plans dynamically, we would need:

$$
v_{t,a}^{p, out} \leq v_{max}, \quad \forall t, a, p
$$
$$
v_{t,a}^{p, in} \geq v_{min}, \quad \forall t, a, p
$$
$$
\frac{(v_{t,a}^{p, out})^2 - (v_{t,a}^{p, in})^2}{2 L_{a}} \leq a_{max}, \quad \forall t, a, p
$$
$$
\frac{(v_{t,a}^{p, in})^2 - (v_{t,a}^{p, out})^2}{2 L_{a}} \leq b_{max}, \quad \forall t, a, p
$$

*Assumption: The set $P_{t,a}$ is generated offline to include only feasible profiles that satisfy these physics constraints.*

#### 6.7. Rerouting Capacity Constraints

If multiple trains reroute to the opposite track, they must also satisfy headway constraints on that track. This is handled by the general conflict resolution constraints (6.4) applied to the opposite track $a_{opp}$.

---

### 7. Model Summary

The model is a MILP with:
*   **Objective:** Minimize weighted sum of delays and energy.
*   **Variables:** Continuous times/energies, binary plan selections, binary ordering variables, binary disruption indicators.
*   **Constraints:**
    1.  Exactly one speed plan per arc.
    2.  Time-linking (arrival/departure/running time consistency).
    3.  Dwell time bounds.
    4.  Disruption logic (rerouting or waiting).
    5.  Headway constraints (arc and node) using Big-M linearization.
    6.  Delay definitions.
    7.  Physical feasibility of speed plans (pre-computed).

This model captures the interdependency between rescheduling (times, orders, routes) and speed management (energy, running times) under disruption, as described in the input. The "train plan selection" approach mentioned in the text is reflected in the use of discrete speed profiles $P_{t,a}$, which allows the model to remain linear.

# Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) under Partial Segment Blockage — MILP Model

## 1. Problem Description and Assumptions

**Problem:** A high-speed railway line experiences a partial segment blockage, where one track in a specific arc is unavailable during a time window. The model simultaneously optimizes train rescheduling (arrival/departure times, ordering, rerouting) and speed management (selection of energy-efficient speed profiles) to produce a conflict-free, energy-efficient recovery timetable.

**Assumptions:**
- **A1:** The railway line is linear with stations $S = \{1, \ldots, |S|\}$ and arcs $A$ connecting consecutive stations.
- **A2:** Each arc has two tracks (one per direction). In the disruption area, one track is blocked, and affected trains may reroute to the opposite track.
- **A3:** Speed profiles are precomputed for each train-arc pair, respecting speed limits, acceleration/deceleration limits, and minimum/maximum running times. The MILP selects from these profiles.
- **A4:** Overtaking is only permitted at stations, not on arcs.
- **A5:** The disruption window is $[T_{dis\_start}, T_{dis\_end}]$. Trains rerouting in the disruption area must traverse the affected arc within this window.
- **A6:** Trains are divided into two directional sets: $T_{up}$ (up-direction) and $T_{down}$ (down-direction).
- **A7:** The planning horizon is finite, bounded by $[0, T_{max}]$.
- **A8:** All trains must complete their journey within the planning horizon.

---

## 2. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $T$ | Set of all trains, $T = T_{up} \cup T_{down}$ |
| $T_{up}$ | Set of trains traveling in the up direction |
| $T_{down}$ | Set of trains traveling in the down direction |
| $S = \{1, \ldots, |S|\}$ | Set of stations, ordered along the line |
| $A$ | Set of arcs; arc $a$ connects station $s$ to station $s+1$ |
| $D \subseteq A$ | Set of disruption-affected arcs |
| $P_{t,a}$ | Set of feasible precomputed speed profiles for train $t$ on arc $a$ |
| $T_{same}(a)$ | Set of unordered pairs $\{t_1, t_2\}$ of trains traveling in the same direction on arc $a$ |
| $T_{opp}(a)$ | Set of unordered pairs $\{t_1, t_2\}$ of trains traveling in opposite directions on arc $a$ (relevant for $a \in D$) |

---

## 3. Parameters

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $RT_{t,a,p}$ | Running time of train $t$ on arc $a$ using speed profile $p$ |
| $E_{t,a,p}$ | Energy consumption of train $t$ on arc $a$ using speed profile $p$ |
| $DwellMin_{t,s}$ | Minimum dwell time of train $t$ at station $s$ |
| $DwellMax_{t,s}$ | Maximum dwell time of train $t$ at station $s$ |
| $HeadwayMin_{a}$ | Minimum headway between consecutive trains on arc $a$ |
| $T_{dis\_start}$ | Start time of the disruption window |
| $T_{dis\_end}$ | End time of the disruption window |
| $T_{max}$ | Planning horizon (maximum time) |
| $ScheduledArr_{t,s}$ | Original scheduled arrival time of train $t$ at station $s$ |
| $ScheduledDep_{t,s}$ | Original scheduled departure time of train $t$ from station $s$ |
| $c_{delay}$ | Penalty coefficient per unit time of delay |
| $c_{energy}$ | Penalty coefficient per unit of energy |
| $c_{reroute}$ | Penalty coefficient for rerouting a train in a disruption arc |
| $M$ | Sufficiently large constant (Big-M), set to $T_{max}$ |

---

## 4. Decision Variables

### Continuous Variables

| Variable | Domain | Description |
|----------|--------|-------------|
| $x_{t,s}^{arr}$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$ | Arrival time of train $t$ at station $s$ |
| $x_{t,s}^{dep}$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$ | Departure time of train $t$ from station $s$ |
| $d_{t,s}^{arr}$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$ | Arrival delay of train $t$ at station $s$ (auxiliary) |
| $d_{t,s}^{dep}$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$ | Departure delay of train $t$ from station $s$ (auxiliary) |

### Binary Variables

| Variable | Domain | Description |
|----------|--------|-------------|
| $z_{t,a,p}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $t$ uses speed profile $p$ on arc $a$ |
| $y_{t,a}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $t$ reroutes to the opposite track in disruption arc $a$ (defined for $a \in D$ only) |
| $w_{t_1,t_2,a}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $t_1$ precedes train $t_2$ on arc $a$ (same-direction ordering) |
| $u_{t_1,t_2,s}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $t_1$ overtakes train $t_2$ at station $s$ |
| $c_{t_1,t_2,a}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if trains $t_1$ and $t_2$ are on the same physical track in disruption arc $a$ (conflict indicator) |
| $m_{t_1,t_2,a}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $t_1$ exits arc $a$ before train $t_2$ enters (for mutual exclusion) |

---

## 5. Objective Function

Minimize the total weighted cost of delays, energy consumption, and rerouting:

$$
\min \; Z = c_{delay} \sum_{t \in T} \sum_{s \in S} \left( d_{t,s}^{arr} + d_{t,s}^{dep} \right) + c_{energy} \sum_{t \in T} \sum_{a \in A} \sum_{p \in P_{t,a}} E_{t,a,p} \, z_{t,a,p} + c_{reroute} \sum_{t \in T} \sum_{a \in D} y_{t,a}
$$

---

## 6. Constraints

### 6.1 Speed Profile Selection

Exactly one speed profile is selected for each train on each arc:

$$
\sum_{p \in P_{t,a}} z_{t,a,p} = 1 \quad \forall \, t \in T, \; \forall \, a \in A \tag{1}
$$

### 6.2 Flow Conservation and Timing Linkage

The arrival at the next station equals the departure from the current station plus the running time of the selected profile. For arc $a$ connecting station $s$ to station $s+1$:

$$
x_{t,s+1}^{arr} = x_{t,s}^{dep} + \sum_{p \in P_{t,a}} RT_{t,a,p} \, z_{t,a,p} \quad \forall \, t \in T, \; \forall \, a \in A \tag{2}
$$

### 6.3 Dwell Time Constraints

$$
x_{t,s}^{dep} - x_{t,s}^{arr} \geq DwellMin_{t,s} \quad \forall \, t \in T, \; \forall \, s \in S \tag{3a}
$$

$$
x_{t,s}^{dep} - x_{t,s}^{arr} \leq DwellMax_{t,s} \quad \forall \, t \in T, \; \forall \, s \in S \tag{3b}
$$

### 6.4 Delay Calculation (Linearization)

Arrival delay:

$$
d_{t,s}^{arr} \geq x_{t,s}^{arr} - ScheduledArr_{t,s} \quad \forall \, t \in T, \; \forall \, s \in S \tag{4a}
$$

$$
d_{t,s}^{arr} \geq 0 \quad \forall \, t \in T, \; \forall \, s \in S \tag{4b}
$$

Departure delay:

$$
d_{t,s}^{dep} \geq x_{t,s}^{dep} - ScheduledDep_{t,s} \quad \forall \, t \in T, \; \forall \, s \in S \tag{4c}
$$

$$
d_{t,s}^{dep} \geq 0 \quad \forall \, t \in T, \; \forall \, s \in S \tag{4d}
$$

*(Since the objective minimizes delay, the solver will set $d_{t,s}^{arr} = \max(0, x_{t,s}^{arr} - ScheduledArr_{t,s})$ and similarly for departure.)*

### 6.5 Rerouting Domain

For non-disruption arcs, rerouting is not possible:

$$
y_{t,a} = 0 \quad \forall \, t \in T, \; \forall \, a \in A \setminus D \tag{5a}
$$

For disruption arcs, $y_{t,a} \in \{0,1\}$ is a free binary decision.

### 6.6 Disruption Time Window

If a train reroutes in a disruption arc $a \in D$ (connecting station $s$ to $s+1$), its traversal must occur within the disruption window:

$$
x_{t,s}^{dep} \geq T_{dis\_start} - M(1 - y_{t,a}) \quad \forall \, t \in T, \; \forall \, a \in D \tag{6a}
$$

$$
x_{t,s+1}^{arr} \leq T_{dis\_end} + M(1 - y_{t,a}) \quad \forall \, t \in T, \; \forall \, a \in D \tag{6b}
$$

*(If $y_{t,a} = 0$, the Big-M terms deactivate the constraints. If $y_{t,a} = 1$, the train must enter after $T_{dis\_start}$ and exit before $T_{dis\_end}$.)*

### 6.7 Same-Direction Headway Constraints

For any two trains $t_1, t_2$ traveling in the same direction on arc $a$ (connecting station $s$ to $s+1$), a minimum headway must be maintained. The ordering variable $w_{t_1,t_2,a}$ determines which train goes first:

$$
w_{t_1,t_2,a} + w_{t_2,t_1,a} = 1 \quad \forall \, \{t_1, t_2\} \in T_{same}(a) \tag{7a}
$$

If $t_1$ precedes $t_2$ ($w_{t_1,t_2,a} = 1$):

$$
x_{t_2,s}^{dep} \geq x_{t_1,s}^{dep} + HeadwayMin_{a} - M(1 - w_{t_1,t_2,a}) \quad \forall \, \{t_1, t_2\} \in T_{same}(a) \tag{7b}
$$

If $t_2$ precedes $t_1$ ($w_{t_2,t_1,a} = 1$):

$$
x_{t_1,s}^{dep} \geq x_{t_2,s}^{dep} + HeadwayMin_{a} - M(1 - w_{t_2,t_1,a}) \quad \forall \, \{t_1, t_2\} \in T_{same}(a) \tag{7c}
$$

**Note for disruption arcs:** For $a \in D$, the headway constraint applies only when both trains are on the **same physical track**. This is handled by the conflict indicator in Section 6.8. For same-direction trains in disruption arcs, the headway constraint is modified:

$$
x_{t_2,s}^{dep} \geq x_{t_1,s}^{dep} + HeadwayMin_{a} - M(1 - w_{t_1,t_2,a}) - M(1 - st_{t_1,t_2,a}) \quad \forall \, \{t_1, t_2\} \in T_{same}(a), \; a \in D \tag{7d}
$$

$$
x_{t_1,s}^{dep} \geq x_{t_2,s}^{dep} + HeadwayMin_{a} - M(1 - w_{t_2,t_1,a}) - M(1 - st_{t_1,t_2,a}) \quad \forall \, \{t_1, t_2\} \in T_{same}(a), \; a \in D \tag{7e}
$$

where $st_{t_1,t_2,a} \in \{0,1\}$ is 1 if $t_1$ and $t_2$ are on the same track in arc $a$, defined by:

$$
st_{t_1,t_2,a} \geq 1 - y_{t_1,a} - y_{t_2,a} \tag{7f}
$$
$$
st_{t_1,t_2,a} \geq y_{t_1,a} + y_{t_2,a} - 1 \tag{7g}
$$
$$
st_{t_1,t_2,a} \leq 1 - y_{t_1,a} + y_{t_2,a} \tag{7h}
$$
$$
st_{t_1,t_2,a} \leq y_{t_1,a} - y_{t_2,a} + 1 \tag{7i}
$$

*(These four constraints linearize $st_{t_1,t_2,a} = 1 - |y_{t_1,a} - y_{t_2,a}|$, i.e., $st = 1$ if both are on the same track.)*

### 6.8 Opposite-Direction Mutual Exclusion in Disruption Area

For trains $t_1 \in T_{up}$ and $t_2 \in T_{down}$ on a disruption arc $a \in D$, a conflict arises when they are on the **same physical track**. This occurs when $y_{t_1,a} \neq y_{t_2,a}$ (one reroutes and the other does not).

**Step 1: Conflict Indicator**

Define $c_{t_1,t_2,a} \in \{0,1\}$ as 1 if $t_1$ and $t_2$ are on the same physical track:

$$
c_{t_1,t_2,a} \geq y_{t_1,a} - y_{t_2,a} \quad \forall \, t_1 \in T_{up}, \; t_2 \in T_{down}, \; a \in D \tag{8a}
$$

$$
c_{t_1,t_2,a} \geq y_{t_2,a} - y_{t_1,a} \quad \forall \, t_1 \in T_{up}, \; t_2 \in T_{down}, \; a \in D \tag{8b}
$$

$$
c_{t_1,t_2,a} \leq y_{t_1,a} + y_{t_2,a} \quad \forall \, t_1 \in T_{up}, \; t_2 \in T_{down}, \; a \in D \tag{8c}
$$

$$
c_{t_1,t_2,a} \leq 2 - y_{t_1,a} - y_{t_2,a} \quad \forall \, t_1 \in T_{up}, \; t_2 \in T_{down}, \; a \in D \tag{8d}
$$

*(This linearizes $c_{t_1,t_2,a} = |y_{t_1,a} - y_{t_2,a}|$, i.e., $c = 1$ if they are on the same track.)*

**Step 2: Temporal Separation**

If $c_{t_1,t_2,a} = 1$, the trains must not be on the arc simultaneously. Let $Entry_{t,a} = x_{t,s}^{dep}$ and $Exit_{t,a} = x_{t,s+1}^{arr}$ for arc $a$ connecting $s$ to $s+1$. Using the sequencing variable $m_{t_1,t_2,a}$:

$$
x_{t_1,s+1}^{arr} \leq x_{t_2,s}^{dep} + M(1 - c_{t_1,t_2,a}) + M(1 - m_{t_1,t_2,a}) \quad \forall \, t_1 \in T_{up}, \; t_2 \in T_{down}, \; a \in D \tag{8e}
$$

$$
x_{t_2,s+1}^{arr} \leq x_{t_1,s}^{dep} + M(1 - c_{t_1,t_2,a}) + M \cdot m_{t_1,t_2,a} \quad \forall \, t_1 \in T_{up}, \; t_2 \in T_{down}, \; a \in D \tag{8f}
$$

*(If $c = 0$, the constraints are non-binding. If $c = 1$, either $t_1$ exits before $t_2$ enters ($m=0$) or $t_2$ exits before $t_1$ enters ($m=1$), preventing head-on collision.)*

### 6.9 Overtaking Constraints

Overtaking is only allowed at stations. If train $t_1$ overtakes train $t_2$ at station $s$, then on the arc $a_{prev}$ ending at $s$, $t_2$ must precede $t_1$, and on the arc $a_{next}$ starting at $s$, $t_1$ must precede $t_2$:

$$
w_{t_2,t_1,a_{prev}} \geq u_{t_1,t_2,s} \quad \forall \, t_1, t_2 \in T, \; \forall \, s \in S \setminus \{1, |S|\} \tag{9a}
$$

$$
w_{t_1,t_2,a_{next}} \geq u_{t_1,t_2,s} \quad \forall \, t_1, t_2 \in T, \; \forall \, s \in S \setminus \{1, |S|\} \tag{9b}
$$

where $a_{prev}$ is the arc ending at station $s$ and $a_{next}$ is the arc starting at station $s$.

### 6.10 Planning Horizon Bounds

All train times must fall within the planning horizon:

$$
0 \leq x_{t,s}^{arr} \leq T_{max} \quad \forall \, t \in T, \; \forall \, s \in S \tag{10a}
$$

$$
0 \leq x_{t,s}^{dep} \leq T_{max} \quad \forall \, t \in T, \; \forall \, s \in S \tag{10b}
$$

### 6.11 Domain Constraints

$$
x_{t,s}^{arr}, \; x_{t,s}^{dep}, \; d_{t,s}^{arr}, \; d_{t,s}^{dep} \geq 0 \quad \forall \, t \in T, \; \forall \, s \in S \tag{11a}
$$

$$
z_{t,a,p} \in \{0,1\} \quad \forall \, t \in T, \; \forall \, a \in A, \; \forall \, p \in P_{t,a} \tag{11b}
$$

$$
y_{t,a} \in \{0,1\} \quad \forall \, t \in T, \; \forall \, a \in D \tag{11c}
$$

$$
w_{t_1,t_2,a} \in \{0,1\} \quad \forall \, t_1, t_2 \in T, \; \forall \, a \in A \tag{11d}
$$

$$
u_{t_1,t_2,s} \in \{0,1\} \quad \forall \, t_1, t_2 \in T, \; \forall \, s \in S \tag{11e}
$$

$$
c_{t_1,t_2,a} \in \{0,1\} \quad \forall \, t_1 \in T_{up}, \; t_2 \in T_{down}, \; \forall \, a \in D \tag{11f}
$$

$$
m_{t_1,t_2,a} \in \{0,1\} \quad \forall \, t_1 \in T_{up}, \; t_2 \in T_{down}, \; \forall \, a \in D \tag{11g}
$$

$$
st_{t_1,t_2,a} \in \{0,1\} \quad \forall \, t_1, t_2 \in T, \; \forall \, a \in D \tag{11h}
$$

## 7. Model Summary

| Component | Role |
|-----------|------|
| **Objective** | Minimizes weighted sum of total delay, energy consumption, and rerouting penalties |
| **Constraints (1)** | Ensures exactly one speed profile per train-arc |
| **Constraints (2)** | Links station times to arc running times via selected profiles |
| **Constraints (3)** | Enforces minimum/maximum dwell times at stations |
| **Constraints (4)** | Linearizes delay as the positive deviation from schedule |
| **Constraints (5)–(6)** | Models rerouting decisions and restricts them to the disruption window |
| **Constraints (7)** | Enforces same-direction headway, activated only when trains share a track |
| **Constraints (8)** | Enforces mutual exclusion for opposite-direction trains on the same physical track in the disruption area |
| **Constraints (9)** | Restricts overtaking to stations only |
| **Constraints (10)–(11)** | Domain and horizon bounds |

**Key Features:**
- The model is fully linear (MILP), with all nonlinearities (speed dynamics, energy) precomputed into the profile set $P_{t,a}$.
- The rerouting variable $y_{t,a}$ couples the rescheduling and conflict-resolution logic: it determines which physical track a train uses, which in turn activates or deactivates headway and mutual-exclusion constraints.
- The conflict indicator $c_{t_1,t_2,a}$ is linearized using four linear inequalities, avoiding the need for product-of-binaries terms.
- The model simultaneously optimizes **when** trains run (rescheduling), **where** they run (rerouting), **in what order** (ordering/overtaking), and **how fast** they run (speed profile selection), yielding a conflict-free, energy-efficient recovery timetable.

Text:
Based on the provided input, here is a complete Mixed-Integer Linear Programming (MILP) model for the **Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP)** under partial segment blockages.

### 1. Problem Description and Assumptions

**Problem Statement:**
The objective is to determine a conflict-free rescheduled timetable and corresponding speed profiles for a set of trains on a high-speed railway line experiencing a partial segment blockage. The model must minimize total operational costs, which include delays, energy consumption, and penalties for rerouting or cancellations.

**Key Assumptions:**
1.  **Network Structure:** The railway line consists of a sequence of stations $S = \{1, 2, \dots, N\}$ and segments $E = \{(i, j) \mid i, j \in S, j = i+1\}$.
2.  **Bidirectional Operation:** Trains operate in two directions (Up and Down). The line has two tracks (Track 1 and Track 2).
3.  **Disruption Scenario:** A specific segment $e_{dis} = (k, k+1)$ is blocked for one direction (e.g., Track 1) during a time window $[T_{start}, T_{end}]$. Trains in the affected direction must reroute to the opposite track (Track 2) or wait.
4.  **Speed Management Discretization:** To maintain linearity, continuous speed profiles are approximated by a finite set of pre-computed "Speed Plans" (or interval plans) for each train on each segment. Each plan defines a specific running time and energy consumption. *Assumption: The set of plans is sufficiently fine-grained to approximate the continuous speed space.*
5.  **Conflict Resolution:** Conflicts are resolved using "Big-M" constraints and binary variables for ordering (who goes first) and track assignment.
6.  **Objective:** Minimize a weighted sum of:
    *   Total passenger delay (deviation from scheduled times).
    *   Total energy consumption.
    *   Penalty for rerouting (using the opposite track).
    *   Penalty for train cancellations.

---

### 2. Sets and Indices

*   $T$: Set of all trains.
*   $T^+$: Set of trains traveling in the "Up" direction.
*   $T^-$: Set of trains traveling in the "Down" direction.
*   $S$: Set of stations, indexed by $s \in \{1, \dots, N\}$.
*   $E$: Set of segments, indexed by $e = (s, s+1)$.
*   $P_{t,e}$: Set of feasible speed plans for train $t$ on segment $e$.
*   $K$: Set of time intervals (if using a time-space network approach, though here we use event-based variables for clarity).

### 3. Parameters

*   $d_{t,s}^{sch}$: Scheduled arrival time of train $t$ at station $s$.
*   $d_{t,s}^{dep}$: Scheduled departure time of train $t$ from station $s$.
*   $r_{t,e}^{min}, r_{t,e}^{max}$: Minimum and maximum possible running times for train $t$ on segment $e$ (derived from speed limits and dynamics).
*   $E_{t,e,p}$: Energy consumption for train $t$ on segment $e$ using speed plan $p \in P_{t,e}$.
*   $RT_{t,e,p}$: Running time for train $t$ on segment $e$ using speed plan $p \in P_{t,e}$.
*   $D_{t,s}^{min}, D_{t,s}^{max}$: Minimum and maximum dwell times at station $s$ for train $t$.
*   $M$: A sufficiently large constant (Big-M).
*   $w_{delay}$: Weight for delay cost.
*   $w_{energy}$: Weight for energy cost.
*   $w_{reroute}$: Penalty cost for rerouting a train to the opposite track.
*   $w_{cancel}$: Penalty cost for canceling a train.
*   $T_{dis}^{start}, T_{dis}^{end}$: Start and end times of the disruption on segment $e_{dis}$.
*   $Track_{t,e}$: The default track for train $t$ on segment $e$ (1 or 2).

### 4. Decision Variables

**Binary Variables:**
*   $x_{t,e,p} \in \{0, 1\}$: Equals 1 if train $t$ uses speed plan $p$ on segment $e$, 0 otherwise.
*   $y_{t,s} \in \{0, 1\}$: Equals 1 if train $t$ is canceled, 0 otherwise.
*   $z_{t,e} \in \{0, 1\}$: Equals 1 if train $t$ is rerouted to the opposite track on segment $e$, 0 otherwise.
*   $u_{t,t',e} \in \{0, 1\}$: Equals 1 if train $t$ precedes train $t'$ on segment $e$ (i.e., $t$ enters the segment before $t'$), 0 otherwise. *Note: This is only defined for pairs of trains that share a segment and potentially conflict.*
*   $v_{t,s} \in \{0, 1\}$: Equals 1 if train $t$ arrives at station $s$ before train $t'$ (for station conflicts).

**Continuous Variables:**
*   $A_{t,s} \ge 0$: Actual arrival time of train $t$ at station $s$.
*   $D_{t,s} \ge 0$: Actual departure time of train $t$ from station $s$.
*   $R_{t,e} \ge 0$: Actual running time of train $t$ on segment $e$.
*   $W_{t,s} \ge 0$: Actual dwell time of train $t$ at station $s$.
*   $Delay_{t,s}^{arr} \ge 0$: Delay of train $t$ at arrival at station $s$.
*   $Delay_{t,s}^{dep} \ge 0$: Delay of train $t$ at departure from station $s$.

---

### 5. Objective Function

Minimize the total cost $Z$:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\min Z = \quad & w_{delay} \sum_{t \in T} \sum_{s \in S} (Delay_{t,s}^{arr} + Delay_{t,s}^{dep}) \\
& + w_{energy} \sum_{t \in T} \sum_{e \in E} \sum_{p \in P_{t,e}} E_{t,e,p} x_{t,e,p} \\
& + w_{reroute} \sum_{t \in T} \sum_{e \in E} z_{t,e} \\
& + w_{cancel} \sum_{t \in T} y_{t,s}
\end{aligned}
$$

*Note: The cancellation penalty is typically applied once per train, so the sum over $s$ for $y_{t,s}$ can be simplified to a single variable $y_t$ if cancellation is a global decision, or kept per station if partial cancellation is allowed. Here we assume global cancellation $y_t$.*

$$
\text{Revised Objective: } \min Z = w_{delay} \sum_{t \in T} \sum_{s \in S} (Delay_{t,s}^{arr} + Delay_{t,s}^{dep}) + w_{energy} \sum_{t \in T} \sum_{e \in E} \sum_{p \in P_{t,e}} E_{t,e,p} x_{t,e,p} + w_{reroute} \sum_{t \in T} \sum_{e \in E} z_{t,e} + w_{cancel} \sum_{t \in T} y_t
$$

---

### 6. Constraints

#### 6.1. Train Operation and Speed Plan Selection

1.  **Single Plan Selection:** Each active train must select exactly one speed plan for each segment.
    $$
    \sum_{p \in P_{t,e}} x_{t,e,p} = 1 - y_t \quad \forall t \in T, e \in E
    $$

2.  **Running Time Determination:** The actual running time is determined by the selected plan.
    $$
    R_{t,e} = \sum_{p \in P_{t,e}} RT_{t,e,p} x_{t,e,p} \quad \forall t \in T, e \in E
    $$

3.  **Energy Consumption Determination:** (Implicit in objective, but can be defined if needed for reporting).

#### 6.2. Time-Linking Constraints (Flow Conservation)

4.  **Departure from Station:** Departure time is Arrival time plus Dwell time.
    $$
    D_{t,s} = A_{t,s} + W_{t,s} \quad \forall t \in T, s \in S
    $$

5.  **Arrival at Next Station:** Arrival at station $s+1$ is Departure from station $s$ plus Running time on segment $(s, s+1)$.
    $$
    A_{t,s+1} = D_{t,s} + R_{t,s,s+1} \quad \forall t \in T, s \in \{1, \dots, N-1\}
    $$

6.  **Dwell Time Bounds:**
    $$
    D_{t,s}^{min} \le W_{t,s} \le D_{t,s}^{max} \quad \forall t \in T, s \in S
    $$

7.  **Cancellation Logic:** If a train is canceled, its times are irrelevant (or set to 0). We use Big-M to deactivate constraints for canceled trains.
    $$
    A_{t,s} \le M(1 - y_t) \quad \forall t \in T, s \in S
    $$
    $$
    D_{t,s} \le M(1 - y_t) \quad \forall t \in T, s \in S
    $$

#### 6.3. Delay Calculation

8.  **Arrival Delay:**
    $$
    Delay_{t,s}^{arr} \ge A_{t,s} - d_{t,s}^{sch} \quad \forall t \in T, s \in S
    $$
    $$
    Delay_{t,s}^{arr} \ge 0
    $$

9.  **Departure Delay:**
    $$
    Delay_{t,s}^{dep} \ge D_{t,s} - d_{t,s}^{dep} \quad \forall t \in T, s \in S
    $$
    $$
    Delay_{t,s}^{dep} \ge 0
    $$

#### 6.4. Disruption and Rerouting Constraints

10. **Rerouting Decision:** A train can only reroute if it is affected by the disruption. Let $Affected(t, e)$ be 1 if train $t$ is in the direction blocked on segment $e$ during the disruption window.
    $$
    z_{t,e} \le Affected(t, e) \quad \forall t \in T, e \in E
    $$

11. **Disruption Time Window Constraint:** If a train is *not* rerouted ($z_{t,e}=0$) and is in the blocked direction, it cannot traverse the segment during the disruption window.
    Let $Entry_{t,e}$ be the time train $t$ enters segment $e$. $Entry_{t,e} = D_{t,s}$ for segment $(s, s+1)$.
    
    If $z_{t,e} = 0$ and $Affected(t, e) = 1$:
    The train must either enter before $T_{dis}^{start}$ or enter after $T_{dis}^{end}$.
    
    Using binary variables $b_{t,e}^{early}$ and $b_{t,e}^{late}$:
    $$
    Entry_{t,e} \le T_{dis}^{start} + M(1 - b_{t,e}^{early}) + M z_{t,e} \quad \forall t \in T, e = e_{dis}
    $$
    $$
    Entry_{t,e} \ge T_{dis}^{end} - M b_{t,e}^{early} + M z_{t,e} \quad \forall t \in T, e = e_{dis}
    $$
    $$
    b_{t,e}^{early} + b_{t,e}^{late} \le 1 + z_{t,e} \quad \text{(If rerouted, this constraint is relaxed)}
    $$
    *Simplification:* If $z_{t,e}=1$, the train uses the opposite track, so the blockage on its original track does not apply. If $z_{t,e}=0$, it must respect the blockage.

#### 6.5. Conflict Resolution (Track and Station)

**A. Segment Conflicts (Bidirectional Trains on Shared Track)**

When two trains $t$ and $t'$ share a segment $e$ and potentially use the same physical track (either by default or due to rerouting), they cannot be on the segment simultaneously.

Let $Track_{t,e}^{actual}$ be the track used.
$Track_{t,e}^{actual} = Track_{t,e}^{default} + z_{t,e}$ (if default is 1, reroute makes it 2; if default is 2, reroute makes it 1). *Assumption: Reroute flips the track.*

If $Track_{t,e}^{actual} = Track_{t',e}^{actual}$, they conflict.

12. **Ordering on Segment:** For any pair of trains $t, t'$ that share a segment $e$ and have the same actual track, one must precede the other.
    $$
    u_{t,t',e} + u_{t',t,e} = 1 \quad \forall t, t' \in T, t \neq t', e \in E \text{ where } Track_{t,e}^{actual} = Track_{t',e}^{actual}
    $$
    *Note: In a linear model, we often define $u_{t,t',e}$ for all pairs and use Big-M to enforce the time separation only if they share the track.*

    **Time Separation Constraint:**
    If $u_{t,t',e} = 1$ (t precedes t'), then $t$ must exit the segment before $t'$ enters.
    $$
    D_{t,s} + R_{t,e} \le D_{t',s} + M(1 - u_{t,t',e}) + M(1 - \mathbb{I}_{same\_track}) \quad \forall t, t', e
    $$
    Where $\mathbb{I}_{same\_track}$ is 1 if they use the same track. To linearize $\mathbb{I}_{same\_track}$, we can use the rerouting variables.
    
    *Simplified Linear Formulation for Conflict:*
    Assume we define $u_{t,t',e}$ for all pairs.
    $$
    A_{t,s+1} \le D_{t',s} + M(1 - u_{t,t',e}) + M \cdot \delta_{t,t',e}
    $$
    $$
    A_{t',s+1} \le D_{t,s} + M u_{t,t',e} + M \cdot \delta_{t,t',e}
    $$
    Where $\delta_{t,t',e}$ is 1 if they do **not** share the same track (no conflict), and 0 if they do.
    
    To define $\delta_{t,t',e}$ linearly:
    Let $k_{t,e} \in \{0,1\}$ be the track index (1 or 2).
    $k_{t,e} = 1 + z_{t,e}$ (assuming default track 1 for Up, 2 for Down, and reroute flips it).
    Conflict exists if $k_{t,e} = k_{t',e}$.
    
    This is complex to linearize directly. A common approximation in MILP is to assume that **all** trains on a segment must be ordered if they are in the same direction, and **bidirectional** trains on the same track must be ordered.
    
    *Alternative Standard Approach:*
    For any pair $t, t'$ on segment $e$:
    If they are in the **same direction**, they must be ordered (no overtaking).
    If they are in **opposite directions**, they conflict only if they use the same track.
    
    Let's use the following Big-M constraints for all pairs $t, t'$ on segment $e$:
    $$
    A_{t,s+1} \le D_{t',s} + M(1 - u_{t,t',e}) + M \cdot (1 - \text{Conflict}_{t,t',e})
    $$
    $$
    A_{t',s+1} \le D_{t,s} + M u_{t,t',e} + M \cdot (1 - \text{Conflict}_{t,t',e})
    $$
    Where $\text{Conflict}_{t,t',e} = 1$ if they share the track.
    
    To avoid non-linear product of binaries, we can assume a conservative approach: **All trains on a segment must be sequenced.** This is valid for single-track sections or when bidirectional traffic is strictly separated by time. However, for bidirectional double-track, this is too restrictive.
    
    *Refined Linearization for Bidirectional Conflict:*
    We introduce binary variable $c_{t,t',e}$ which is 1 if trains $t$ and $t'$ conflict on segment $e$.
    $$
    c_{t,t',e} \ge z_{t,e} + z_{t',e} - 1 \quad \text{(If both reroute, they might meet on the "other" track)}
    $$
    $$
    c_{t,t',e} \ge 1 - z_{t,e} - z_{t',e} \quad \text{(If neither reroutes, they are on default tracks. If default tracks are different, no conflict. If same, conflict.)}
    $$
    *This is getting complex. Let's assume the standard "Time-Table" approach where we enforce separation for all pairs that could potentially share a track.*
    
    **Simplifying Assumption for Model Completeness:**
    We assume that for any pair of trains $t, t'$ on segment $e$, if they are in opposite directions, they **must** be ordered (one enters before the other exits) to ensure safety, regardless of track, unless we explicitly model track separation. Given the prompt mentions "bidirectional trains sharing track resources," we must model the track sharing.
    
    Let's use the following constraint set for any pair $t, t'$ on segment $e$:
    $$
    A_{t,s+1} \le D_{t',s} + M(1 - u_{t,t',e}) + M \cdot \gamma_{t,t',e}
    $$
    $$
    A_{t',s+1} \le D_{t,s} + M u_{t,t',e} + M \cdot \gamma_{t,t',e}
    $$
    Where $\gamma_{t,t',e}$ is 1 if they do **not** conflict (i.e., they are on different tracks).
    
    To linearize $\gamma_{t,t',e}$:
    Let $k_{t,e}$ be the track used.
    $k_{t,e} = 1 + z_{t,e}$ (for Up trains, default 1, reroute 2).
    $k_{t,e} = 2 - z_{t,e}$ (for Down trains, default 2, reroute 1).
    
    Conflict if $k_{t,e} = k_{t',e}$.
    
    This requires auxiliary variables to compare $k_{t,e}$ and $k_{t',e}$.
    
    **Practical MILP Formulation (Common in Literature):**
    Often, the model enforces that **no two trains can be on the same segment at the same time** if they are in the same direction. For opposite directions, it enforces that they cannot be on the **same track** at the same time.
    
    Let's define the constraint for **Same Direction** (e.g., $t, t' \in T^+$):
    $$
    A_{t,s+1} \le D_{t',s} + M(1 - u_{t,t',e})
    $$
    $$
    A_{t',s+1} \le D_{t,s} + M u_{t,t',e}
    $$
    (They must be ordered).
    
    For **Opposite Directions** ($t \in T^+, t' \in T^-$):
    They conflict only if they use the same track.
    Let $s_{t,t',e}$ be 1 if they use the same track.
    $$
    s_{t,t',e} \ge z_{t,e} + z_{t',e} - 1
    $$
    $$
    s_{t,t',e} \ge 1 - z_{t,e} - z_{t',e}
    $$
    $$
    s_{t,t',e} \le z_{t,e} + z_{t',e}
    $$
    $$
    s_{t,t',e} \le 2 - z_{t,e} - z_{t',e}
    $$
    *Wait, this logic depends on default tracks.*
    If $t$ is Up (Default 1) and $t'$ is Down (Default 2):
    - If $z_{t,e}=0, z_{t',e}=0$: Tracks 1 and 2. No conflict. $s=0$.
    - If $z_{t,e}=1, z_{t',e}=0$: Tracks 2 and 2. Conflict. $s=1$.
    - If $z_{t,e}=0, z_{t',e}=1$: Tracks 1 and 1. Conflict. $s=1$.
    - If $z_{t,e}=1, z_{t',e}=1$: Tracks 2 and 1. No conflict. $s=0$.
    
    So, $s_{t,t',e} = 1$ if $z_{t,e} \neq z_{t',e}$.
    $$
    s_{t,t',e} \ge z_{t,e} - z_{t',e}
    $$
    $$
    s_{t,t',e} \ge z_{t',e} - z_{t,e}
    $$
    $$
    s_{t,t',e} \le 1 - z_{t,e} + z_{t',e}
    $$
    $$
    s_{t,t',e} \le 1 + z_{t,e} - z_{t',e}
    $$
    
    Now, apply the time separation only if $s_{t,t',e} = 1$:
    $$
    A_{t,s+1} \le D_{t',s} + M(1 - u_{t,t',e}) + M(1 - s_{t,t',e})
    $$
    $$
    A_{t',s+1} \le D_{t,s} + M u_{t,t',e} + M(1 - s_{t,t',e})
    $$
    And ensure ordering is defined:
    $$
    u_{t,t',e} + u_{t',t,e} = 1 \quad \text{(Only if } s_{t,t',e}=1 \text{? No, usually defined for all, but relaxed if no conflict)}
    $$
    Actually, if $s_{t,t',e}=0$, the Big-M term $M(1-s)$ becomes $M$, making the constraint non-binding. So we can keep $u_{t,t',e} + u_{t',t,e} = 1$ for all pairs, or just define $u$ for conflicting pairs. For simplicity, we define $u$ for all pairs.

**B. Station Conflicts**

Trains cannot arrive/depart at the same station simultaneously if the station has limited platforms. Assume 1 platform per direction.

13. **Station Ordering:** For any pair $t, t'$ at station $s$ in the same direction:
    $$
    D_{t,s} \le A_{t',s} + M(1 - v_{t,t',s})
    $$
    $$
    D_{t',s} \le A_{t,s} + M v_{t,t',s}
    $$
    $$
    v_{t,t',s} + v_{t',t,s} = 1
    $$
    (Train $t$ must depart before train $t'$ arrives, or vice versa).

    For opposite directions, if they share a platform (rare in HS, usually separate), similar logic applies. We assume separate platforms for Up/Down, so no conflict between $T^+$ and $T^-$ at stations.

#### 6.6. Boundary Conditions

14. **Initial Times:**
    $$
    A_{t,1} \ge 0
    $$
    $$
    D_{t,N} \le T_{horizon}
    $$

15. **Non-negativity:**
    All continuous variables $\ge 0$.
    All binary variables $\in \{0, 1\}$.

---

### 7. Summary of the Model

This MILP model integrates:
1.  **Rescheduling:** Via variables $A_{t,s}, D_{t,s}$ and delay penalties.
2.  **Speed Management:** Via discrete speed plans $x_{t,e,p}$ and energy penalties.
3.  **Rerouting:** Via binary variables $z_{t,e}$ and disruption constraints.
4.  **Conflict Resolution:** Via Big-M constraints for segment and station ordering, with specific logic for bidirectional track sharing during rerouting.

**Solution Approach Note:**
As mentioned in the input, this model is computationally heavy. The proposed solution method involves decomposing this into an IP model for train interactions (ordering/routing) and a series of train plans (speed/energy optimization for fixed times), solved iteratively. The MILP above represents the **integrated master problem** that the decomposition method approximates.

# Mixed-Integer Linear Programming Model for the Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) under Partial Segment Blockage

## 1. Problem Description and Assumptions

**Problem:** A high-speed railway line experiences a partial blockage in one segment, where one direction of track is unavailable during a known time window. The operator must simultaneously reschedule trains (adjusting times, ordering, rerouting, and possibly cancelling) and determine speed profiles (running times) to minimize total passenger delay, energy consumption, and cancellation penalties, while ensuring a conflict-free timetable.

**Assumptions:**
1. The railway is a single bidirectional line with stations $S = \{1, 2, \ldots, |S|\}$ in sequence.
2. A single segment $d$ (between stations $d$ and $d+1$) is partially blocked in direction $d_{blocked}$ during time window $[t_{start}, t_{end}]$.
3. Trains in the blocked direction may be rerouted to the opposite track in segment $d$ during the disruption window.
4. Speed profiles are approximated by a finite set of discrete options $K$ per segment, each with a fixed running time and energy cost (piecewise-linear approximation of the non-linear energy–time relationship).
5. Trains cannot overtake on segments (block-based signaling).
6. Each station has a single platform per direction; trains must be sequenced at stations.
7. The planning horizon is $[0, H]$.
8. Passenger counts $p_t$ are fixed and known.
9. Minimum and maximum dwell times and headways are known constants.
10. Trains may be cancelled as a last resort.

---

## 2. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $T$ | Set of all trains, $T = \{1, \ldots, |T|\}$ |
| $T_{dir}$ | Subset of trains traveling in the blocked direction |
| $T_{opp}$ | Subset of trains traveling in the opposite direction |
| $S$ | Set of stations, $S = \{1, \ldots, |S|\}$ |
| $L$ | Set of track segments, $L = \{1, \ldots, |S|-1\}$; segment $j$ connects station $j$ to $j+1$ |
| $K$ | Set of speed profile options per segment, $K = \{1, \ldots, |K|\}$ |
| $d$ | Index of the disrupted segment |
| $T_{max}$ | Planning horizon |

---

## 3. Parameters

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $p_t$ | Number of passengers on train $t$ |
| $w_t$ | Delay weight for train $t$ (typically $w_t = p_t$) |
| $c_{cancel}$ | Penalty cost for cancelling a train |
| $w_E$ | Weight for energy consumption in the objective |
| $rt_{j,k}$ | Running time on segment $j$ under speed profile $k$ |
| $e_{j,k}$ | Energy consumption on segment $j$ under speed profile $k$ |
| $dwell_{min}$ | Minimum dwell time at any station |
| $dwell_{max}$ | Maximum dwell time at any station |
| $h_{min}$ | Minimum headway between consecutive trains on a segment |
| $sep_i$ | Minimum separation time at station $i$ (for station ordering) |
| $A^{orig}_{t,i}$ | Original scheduled arrival time of train $t$ at station $i$ |
| $D^{orig}_{t,i}$ | Original scheduled departure time of train $t$ from station $i$ |
| $t_{start}, t_{end}$ | Start and end of the disruption time window |
| $M$ | Sufficiently large constant (Big-M), set to $T_{max}$ |
| $\epsilon$ | Small positive constant (e.g., 1 second) |

---

## 4. Decision Variables

### Continuous Variables

| Variable | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| $A_{t,i} \geq 0$ | Arrival time of train $t$ at station $i$ |
| $D_{t,i} \geq 0$ | Departure time of train $t$ from station $i$ |
| $RT_{t,j} \geq 0$ | Running time of train $t$ on segment $j$ |
| $E_{t,j} \geq 0$ | Energy consumption of train $t$ on segment $j$ |
| $Delay_{t,i} \geq 0$ | Delay of train $t$ at station $i$ relative to original schedule |

### Binary Variables

| Variable | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| $x_{t,j,k} \in \{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $t$ uses speed profile $k$ on segment $j$ |
| $y_t \in \{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $t$ is cancelled |
| $r_t \in \{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $t$ is rerouted to the opposite track in segment $d$ (only for $t \in T_{dir}$) |
| $w_t \in \{0,1\}$ | Auxiliary: 1 if train $t$ traverses segment $d$ before $t_{start}$; 0 if after $t_{end}$ (only for $t \in T_{dir}$ with $r_t = 0$) |
| $u_{t,t',i} \in \{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $t$ precedes train $t'$ at station $i$ |
| $v_{t,t',j} \in \{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $t$ precedes train $t'$ on segment $j$ (same direction) |
| $v^{cross}_{t,t'} \in \{0,1\}$ | 1 if rerouted train $t \in T_{dir}$ precedes train $t' \in T_{opp}$ on segment $d$ |

---

## 5. Objective Function

$$
\min \; Z = \sum_{t \in T} \sum_{i \in S} w_t \cdot Delay_{t,i} \;+\; w_E \sum_{t \in T} \sum_{j \in L} E_{t,j} \;+\; c_{cancel} \sum_{t \in T} y_t
$$

**Interpretation:**
- **First term:** Total weighted passenger delay across all stations.
- **Second term:** Total weighted energy consumption across all segments.
- **Third term:** Penalty for cancelled trains.

---

## 6. Constraints

### 6.1. Cancellation Logic

If a train is cancelled, its timing variables are deactivated:

$$
A_{t,i} \leq M(1 - y_t) \quad \forall\, t \in T,\; i \in S \tag{1}
$$

$$
D_{t,i} \leq M(1 - y_t) \quad \forall\, t \in T,\; i \in S \tag{2}
$$

$$
RT_{t,j} \leq M(1 - y_t) \quad \forall\, t \in T,\; j \in L \tag{3}
$$

$$
E_{t,j} \leq M(1 - y_t) \quad \forall\, t \in T,\; j \in L \tag{4}
$$

$$
Delay_{t,i} \leq M \cdot y_t \quad \forall\, t \in T,\; i \in S \tag{5}
$$

*(If $y_t = 1$, all timing variables are forced to 0 and delay is 0.)*

### 6.2. Speed Profile Selection

Each non-cancelled train selects exactly one speed profile per segment:

$$
\sum_{k \in K} x_{t,j,k} = 1 - y_t \quad \forall\, t \in T,\; j \in L \tag{6}
$$

**Running time linkage:**

$$
RT_{t,j} = \sum_{k \in K} rt_{j,k} \cdot x_{t,j,k} \quad \forall\, t \in T,\; j \in L \tag{7}
$$

**Energy consumption linkage:**

$$
E_{t,j} = \sum_{k \in K} e_{j,k} \cdot x_{t,j,k} \quad \forall\, t \in T,\; j \in L \tag{8}
$$

### 6.3. Temporal Consistency (Flow of Time)

**Dwell time at stations:**

$$
D_{t,i} \geq A_{t,i} + dwell_{min} - M \cdot y_t \quad \forall\, t \in T,\; i \in S \tag{9}
$$

$$
D_{t,i} \leq A_{t,i} + dwell_{max} + M \cdot y_t \quad \forall\, t \in T,\; i \in S \tag{10}
$$

**Running time between stations (forward direction, $t \in T_{dir}$):**

$$
A_{t,i+1} = D_{t,i} + RT_{t,i} \quad \forall\, t \in T_{dir},\; i = 1, \ldots, |S|-1 \tag{11}
$$

**Running time between stations (backward direction, $t \in T_{opp}$):**

$$
A_{t,i} = D_{t,i+1} + RT_{t,i+1} \quad \forall\, t \in T_{opp},\; i = 1, \ldots, |S|-1 \tag{12}
$$

*(Note: For cancelled trains, these equalities are relaxed by adding $-M y_t$ on the RHS or by fixing variables to 0 via (1)–(4). In practice, one may write $A_{t,i+1} \geq D_{t,i} + RT_{t,i} - M y_t$ and $A_{t,i+1} \leq D_{t,i} + RT_{t,i} + M y_t$.)*

### 6.4. Delay Calculation

$$
Delay_{t,i} \geq A_{t,i} - A^{orig}_{t,i} \quad \forall\, t \in T,\; i \in S \tag{13}
$$

$$
Delay_{t,i} \geq 0 \quad \forall\, t \in T,\; i \in S \tag{14}
$$

### 6.5. Disruption and Rerouting Constraints

**Rerouting eligibility:**

$$
r_t = 0 \quad \forall\, t \in T_{opp} \tag{15}
$$

$$
r_t \leq 1 - y_t \quad \forall\, t \in T_{dir} \tag{16}
$$

**Disruption time window (for non-rerouted trains on the blocked track):**

If $r_t = 0$, train $t$ must not be on the blocked track during $[t_{start}, t_{end}]$. This is a disjunction: the train must either **finish** segment $d$ before $t_{start}$ or **start** segment $d$ after $t_{end}$.

Using auxiliary binary $w_t$ (1 = before, 0 = after):

$$
A_{t,d+1} \leq t_{start} - \epsilon + M(1 - w_t) + M \cdot r_t + M \cdot y_t \quad \forall\, t \in T_{dir} \tag{17}
$$

$$
D_{t,d} \geq t_{end} + \epsilon - M \cdot w_t + M \cdot r_t + M \cdot y_t \quad \forall\, t \in T_{dir} \tag{18}
$$

**Logic:**
- If $r_t = 1$ (rerouted): the $M \cdot r_t$ terms dominate, making (17)–(18) non-binding. The train uses the opposite track, so the blockage is irrelevant.
- If $r_t = 0$ and $w_t = 1$: (17) becomes $A_{t,d+1} \leq t_{start} - \epsilon$ (must finish before disruption starts); (18) is relaxed.
- If $r_t = 0$ and $w_t = 0$: (18) becomes $D_{t,d} \geq t_{end} + \epsilon$ (must start after disruption ends); (17) is relaxed.

### 6.6. Conflict Resolution

#### 6.6.1. Station Ordering (Dwell Conflicts)

For any pair of trains $t \neq t'$ at station $i$ (both non-cancelled):

$$
D_{t,i} \geq A_{t',i} + sep_i - M(1 - u_{t,t',i}) - M \cdot y_t - M \cdot y_{t'} \quad \forall\, t \neq t',\; i \in S \tag{19}
$$

$$
D_{t',i} \geq A_{t,i} + sep_i - M \cdot u_{t,t',i} - M \cdot y_t - M \cdot y_{t'} \quad \forall\, t \neq t',\; i \in S \tag{20}
$$

$$
u_{t,t',i} + u_{t',t,i} = 1 - y_t - y_{t'} \quad \forall\, t \neq t',\; i \in S \tag{21}
$$

*(If either train is cancelled, the ordering constraint is deactivated.)*

#### 6.6.2. Same-Direction Segment Headways

For any pair of trains $t, t'$ in the **same direction** on segment $j$:

$$
A_{t,j+1} \geq A_{t',j+1} + h_{min} - M(1 - v_{t,t',j}) - M \cdot y_t - M \cdot y_{t'} \quad \forall\, t \neq t',\; j \in L \tag{22}
$$

$$
A_{t',j+1} \geq A_{t,j+1} + h_{min} - M \cdot v_{t,t',j} - M \cdot y_t - M \cdot y_{t'} \quad \forall\, t \neq t',\; j \in L \tag{23}
$$

$$
v_{t,t',j} + v_{t',t,j} = 1 - y_t - y_{t'} \quad \forall\, t \neq t',\; j \in L \tag{24}
$$

*(Only applies to pairs in the same direction. For $j = d$, this applies to trains in $T_{dir}$ that are **not** rerouted, and to trains in $T_{opp}$ on their normal track.)*

#### 6.6.3. Rerouting Conflicts (Bidirectional on Shared Track)

If train $t \in T_{dir}$ is rerouted ($r_t = 1$), it shares the track with trains in $T_{opp}$ on segment $d$. Headway constraints must be enforced:

$$
A_{t,d+1} \geq A_{t',d+1} + h_{min} - M(1 - v^{cross}_{t,t'}) - M(1 - r_t) - M \cdot y_t - M \cdot y_{t'} \quad \forall\, t \in T_{dir},\; t' \in T_{opp} \tag{25}
$$

$$
A_{t',d+1} \geq A_{t,d+1} + h_{min} - M \cdot v^{cross}_{t,t'} - M(1 - r_t) - M \cdot y_t - M \cdot y_{t'} \quad \forall\, t \in T_{dir},\; t' \in T_{opp} \tag{26}
$$

$$
v^{cross}_{t,t'} + v^{cross}_{t',t} = r_t - y_t - y_{t'} \quad \forall\, t \in T_{dir},\; t' \in T_{opp} \tag{27}
$$

**Logic:**
- If $r_t = 0$: the $-M(1 - r_t) = -M$ terms make (25)–(26) non-binding, and (27) forces $v^{cross} = 0$ (no ordering needed since trains are on different tracks).
- If $r_t = 1$: the $-M(1 - r_t) = 0$, and standard headway ordering applies between the rerouted train and opposite-direction trains.

### 6.7. Time Horizon Bounds

$$
0 \leq A_{t,i} \leq T_{max} \quad \forall\, t \in T,\; i \in S \tag{28}
$$

$$
0 \leq D_{t,i} \leq T_{max} \quad \forall\, t \in T,\; i \in S \tag{29}
$$

### 6.8. Variable Domains

$$
x_{t,j,k} \in \{0,1\}, \quad y_t \in \{0,1\}, \quad r_t \in \{0,1\}, \quad w_t \in \{0,1\} \tag{30}
$$

$$
u_{t,t',i} \in \{0,1\}, \quad v_{t,t',j} \in \{0,1\}, \quad v^{cross}_{t,t'} \in \{0,1\} \tag{31}
$$

$$
A_{t,i}, D_{t,i}, RT_{t,j}, E_{t,j}, Delay_{t,i} \geq 0 \tag{32}
$$

---

## 7. Model Summary and Key Features

| Feature | How It Is Handled |
|---------|-------------------|
| **Rescheduling (retiming)** | Continuous variables $A_{t,i}$, $D_{t,i}$ with dwell and running-time constraints |
| **Reordering** | Binary ordering variables $u_{t,t',i}$, $v_{t,t',j}$ with Big-M headway constraints |
| **Rerouting** | Binary $r_t$; if 1, train uses opposite track in segment $d$, triggering cross-direction headway constraints |
| **Cancellation** | Binary $y_t$; Big-M deactivates all timing and conflict constraints for cancelled trains |
| **Speed management** | Discrete speed profiles $K$ per segment; binary $x_{t,j,k}$ selects one profile, linking running time and energy |
| **Energy efficiency** | Energy $E_{t,j}$ is a direct function of the selected speed profile; minimized in the objective |
| **Disruption handling** | Disjunctive constraint (17)–(18) forces non-rerouted trains to avoid the blocked time window |
| **Bidirectional conflicts** | Cross-direction headway constraints (25)–(27) activated only when $r_t = 1$ |
| **Linearity** | All constraints are linear; non-linear energy–time relationship is approximated by discrete profiles |

---

## 8. Implementation Notes

1. **Big-M value:** Set $M = T_{max}$ (the planning horizon in seconds). Tighter bounds improve solver performance.
2. **Speed profile granularity:** The set $K$ should include 5–15 profiles spanning the feasible running-time range. More profiles improve accuracy but increase model size.
3. **Symmetry breaking:** For ordering variables, if train $t$ is originally scheduled before train $t'$, add $v_{t,t',j} \geq v_{t',t,j}$ for initial segments to reduce symmetry.
4. **Initial solution:** A feasible initial solution (e.g., original timetable with no rerouting, or a heuristic solution) can be provided to the solver to accelerate convergence.
5. **Scalability:** For large instances, the decomposition approach described in the paper (splitting into an IP for train interactions and subproblems for individual train plans) can be applied to this MILP as a master problem.

# Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) under Partial Segment Blockage: A Mixed-Integer Linear Programming Model

## 1. Problem Description and Assumptions

This model addresses the integrated optimization of train timetables and speed profiles in a high-speed railway system experiencing a partial segment blockage disruption. The model simultaneously determines train arrival/departure times, inter-station running times (speed profiles), rerouting decisions, train ordering, and potential cancellations to minimize total delay, energy consumption, and operational penalties while ensuring conflict-free operations.

**Assumptions:**
- **A1:** The railway is a single line with $N$ stations and $N-1$ segments.
- **A2:** Trains operate in two directions: up (increasing station index) and down (decreasing station index).
- **A3:** A partial blockage occurs on segment $d_{dis}$ during time window $[T_{dis}^{start}, T_{dis}^{end}]$, blocking the up-direction track.
- **A4:** Affected up-trains can either wait (complete before or start after the disruption), reroute to the opposite (down) track, or be cancelled.
- **A5:** Speed management is modeled via inter-station running times, which determine energy consumption through a linear approximation.
- **A6:** Energy consumption increases as running time decreases (faster speed = higher energy).
- **A7:** Minimum headways must be maintained between trains on the same track.
- **A8:** On the disrupted segment, rerouted up-trains share the track with down-trains, requiring no-overlap constraints.
- **A9:** Station capacity is limited to $C_s$ trains simultaneously (modeled for $C_s = 1$).
- **A10:** The planning horizon is $[0, T_{horizon}]$.
- **A11:** Trains have fixed origins and destinations.
- **A12:** Maximum delay per train is bounded; trains exceeding this are cancelled.

## 2. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $S = \{1, 2, \dots, N\}$ | Set of stations |
| $I = \{1, 2, \dots, N-1\}$ | Set of segments; segment $i$ connects station $i$ and $i+1$ |
| $T$ | Set of all trains |
| $T_{up} \subset T$ | Set of up-direction trains |
| $T_{down} \subset T$ | Set of down-direction trains |
| $d_{dis}$ | Index of the disrupted segment |
| $T_{up,dis} \subset T_{up}$ | Up-trains that traverse segment $d_{dis}$ |
| $T_{down,dis} \subset T_{down}$ | Down-trains that traverse segment $d_{dis}$ |
| $S_t$ | Set of stations visited by train $t$ |
| $I_t$ | Set of segments traversed by train $t$ |
| $O_t$ | Origin station of train $t$ |
| $D_t$ | Destination station of train $t$ |
| $T_{same,i}$ | Set of ordered pairs $(t_1, t_2)$ of same-direction trains both traversing segment $i$ |
| $T_{opp,dis}$ | Set of ordered pairs $(t_{up}, t_{down})$ where $t_{up} \in T_{up,dis}$ and $t_{down} \in T_{down,dis}$ |
| $T_{stop,s}$ | Set of trains that stop at station $s$ |

## 3. Parameters

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $T_{horizon}$ | Planning horizon end time |
| $T_{dis}^{start}, T_{dis}^{end}$ | Start and end times of the disruption on segment $d_{dis}$ |
| $y_{t,i}^{min}, y_{t,i}^{max}$ | Minimum and maximum running times for train $t$ on segment $i$ |
| $\delta_{min}, \delta_{max}$ | Minimum and maximum dwell times at intermediate stations |
| $\alpha_{t,i}, \beta_{t,i}$ | Energy model coefficients for train $t$ on segment $i$ |
| $h_{same}$ | Minimum headway between same-direction trains on a segment |
| $h_{opp}$ | Minimum separation time for opposite-direction trains on shared track |
| $x_{t,s}^{sched,arr}$ | Scheduled arrival time of train $t$ at station $s$ |
| $x_{t,s}^{sched,dep}$ | Scheduled departure time of train $t$ from station $s$ |
| $D_{max}$ | Maximum allowable delay before forced cancellation |
| $C_s$ | Station capacity at station $s$ (assumed $C_s = 1$) |
| $M$ | Sufficiently large constant (Big-M) |
| $w_{delay}, w_{energy}, w_{cancel}, w_{reroute}$ | Objective function weights |

## 4. Decision Variables

### Continuous Variables

| Variable | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| $x_{t,s}^{arr} \geq 0$ | Arrival time of train $t$ at station $s$ |
| $x_{t,s}^{dep} \geq 0$ | Departure time of train $t$ from station $s$ |
| $y_{t,i}^{run} \geq 0$ | Running time of train $t$ on segment $i$ |
| $e_{t,i} \geq 0$ | Energy consumption of train $t$ on segment $i$ |
| $d_{t,s} \geq 0$ | Delay of train $t$ at station $s$ |

### Binary Variables

| Variable | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| $c_t \in \{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $t$ is cancelled |
| $r_{t,d_{dis}} \in \{0,1\}$ | 1 if up-train $t$ is rerouted on segment $d_{dis}$ (only for $t \in T_{up,dis}$) |
